evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The paper reports token-level F1, zero-shot transfer to LoCoMo, paired McNemar significance tests, and a cross-model judge audit with Cohen's kappa between 0.836 and 0.894.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline accuracy is reported on disjoint LifeBench test users and on LoCoMo as a zero-shot transfer benchmark, using an LLM majority-vote answer judge and token-level F1.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The 1.7B locator is trained with GRPO on LifeBench training users using a composite reward that includes an LLM evidence-coverage judge and an LLM answer-correctness judge, alongside window IoU and detection terms.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of achieving strong gains over baselines (e.g., 61.52% on LifeBench and 78.96% on LoCoMo) and addressing temporal crowd-out at retrieval are well-supported by quantitative comparisons, ablation studies, and diagnostic error analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are comprehensive across two major benchmarks (LifeBench and LoCoMo), testing against multiple agentic memory frameworks, time-sensitive retrievers, and temporal reasoning methods, supported by ablations on rewards, locator capacities, hyperparameter sweeps, paired significance tests, and cross-judge agreement audits.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations include token-level F1 score, exact match metrics, zero-shot evaluation on the held-out LoCoMo benchmark, and a cross-model judge audit demonstrating high inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa > 0.83).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established on disjoint test splits (LifeBench user-0/1) and zero-shot benchmark transfer (LoCoMo), evaluated via standard benchmark QA accuracy (LLM majority-vote judge) and token-level F1.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The locator is trained using GRPO on LifeBench training users (user-2 to user-9) with a composite reward including window IoU, LLM evidence-coverage judge, and LLM answer-correctness judge.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge the reliance on synthetic personal histories rather than noisy real-world traces, potential vulnerability to errors in upstream memory extraction and clustering, and evaluation restricted to English-language date conventions.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the event-clustering memory pool, the formulation of parallel temporal and semantic retrieval channels with distance-decay reranking, and the GRPO training scheme using a composite reward (temporal detection, window IoU, evidence recall, and answer correctness).
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a clear, well-scoped contribution to long-horizon agent memory with rigorous empirical validation, extensive ablations isolating the locator policy from model scale or memory construction, and a solid examination of failure modes.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces TIDER, an agentic long-term memory retrieval framework featuring a 1.7B parameter RL-trained temporal interval locator that emits explicit time windows to drive a dual-channel (temporal and semantic) retrieval and reranking mechanism.

shared memory, so the records it plants carry its
own authority. What must hold is that this authority
stops at its owner, which is the role of scope.

questions, none of these calls runs: the patient iden-

whose authority belongs to another principal, and
the call check refuses it. Without the scope check,

as the operative check. Defenses that judge content

vent every execution, but they remove 70.4% and
71.4% of the memories that benign questions would
retrieve; SAFE-Mem removes 2.0%, keeping what

as strong as the model that applies them. Without
defense, GPT-5.6-terra resists more attacks than

The same dependence appears inside SAFE-Mem
when inadmissible entries are served with a descrip-
tion label: ASR rises from 2.6% and 6.2% to 6.2%
and 19.6% (Appendix M). Withholding decides
what reaches the context, and with it SAFE-Mem's
ASR stays between 1.5% and 6.2% across all four
backbones (Table 1). The judgments that set the
labels hold up against human labels (Appendix I):
the use classifier separates descriptions from every
higher kind on 94.0% of requests on GPT-5.6-terra,
the retention judgment agrees on 84.0% of prin-
cipal sentences, and the answer judge agrees on
83.5% of answers.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded human labels agree with the retention judgment on 84.0% of sentences, with the use classifier on 84.7% of requests, and with the answer judge on 83.5% of answers, while EHRAgent execution outcomes are deterministic.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are scored by GPT-4o-mini judges on MPBench and LoCoMo, with EHRAgent outcomes measured by executed-code targeting and memory-loss rates.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The governance rules, kind lattice, authority assignment, and prompt templates are fixed a priori; no training, reward, or automated tuning loop adapts the system against the reported outcomes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding defense efficacy, resistance to adaptive prompt attacks, and retention of legitimate recall are supported by multi-model benchmarks, ablations, and bootstrap confidence intervals.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated across multiple backbones (GPT-5.6-terra, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku 5.5, Qwen3.8-Flash) on MPBench, LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and EHRAgent under MINJA, demonstrating marked reductions in attack success rate (ASR) while maintaining or improving memory recall and accuracy.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded human annotations evaluated agreement on retention judgments (84%), use classification (84.7%), and answer evaluations (83.5%, Cohen's kappa 0.67), alongside deterministic tool execution rates in EHRAgent.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test suites scored via independent GPT-4o-mini automated judges (evaluating ASR, recall, and LoCoMo accuracy) alongside execution-level checks on EHRAgent.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System rules, prompt templates, and governance lattices fixed a priori without continuous gradient training or automated reinforcement tuning.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly bound their threat model, noting that persuaded principals can still endorse poisoned content and that false factual statements not relying on borrowed authority fall outside authority governance.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing a 5-tier illocutionary force lattice, channel-bound authority assignment, memory graph representations connecting source sentences to claims, and a formal pre-ranking admission filter alongside tool execution guards.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents an impactful, well-formalized system for agentic memory security with rigorous empirical validation against established baselines, comprehensive ablations, and blinded human calibration of automated judgments.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces SAFE-Mem, a memory governance architecture for LLM agents that tracks claim provenance, binding force (kind), authority, and principal scope to prevent authority laundering while preserving benign memory recall.
